Customizable China and Global Map Visualizations

Source: R/ggmapcn-package.R
ggmapcn-package.Rd

Provides layers and annotations for drawing maps of China and the world with ggplot2. Supports map projections, administrative boundaries, graticules, scale bars, north arrows, buffer zones, and raster overlays. China administrative division data are derived from the Tianditu geospatial information service, with separate layers for land borders, coastlines, and maritime boundaries.

Map layers

  • World maps: geom_world() draws a global basemap with countries, coastlines, boundaries, and optional ocean fill.

  • China maps: geom_mapcn() and geom_boundary_cn() provide provincial, prefecture-level maps and coastlines.

  • Annotation tools:

    • annotation_graticule() — global graticules with projection-aware labels.

    • annotation_scalebar() — scale bar with automatic units and CRS detection.

    • annotation_compass() — north arrow with several styles.

  • Projection helper:

    • coord_proj() — specify geographic xlim/ylim in degrees and automatically transform to any projection.

Geospatial data

The package provides default boundary, world map, elevation, and vegetation datasets for direct use by its mapping functions. Some files are distributed in the installed package; larger files are hosted in the companion ggmapcn-data repository. check_geodata() reuses local copies or retrieves missing default files. It returns NA for files it cannot retrieve. Mapping functions require the corresponding datasets to be available before plotting.

Integration

Mapping and annotation functions return layers or lists of layers for ggplot2. check_geodata() returns file paths, and coord_proj() returns a coordinate system.
